sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat through FY2022, then stepped up 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which added $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year's total [S61][D604][P48].
FY2026's 17.3% gain was driven by cloud revenue, with cloud infrastructure contributing 84% of constant-currency cloud growth [D421][P17].
Cloud Infrastructure revenue grew 76.9% in FY2026 and contributed 13.7pp of the 17.3% total growth [D644][D645][D421].
Cloud Infrastructure reached 26.9% of revenue in FY2026, up from 12.9% in FY2024 [D643][D639].
The Americas contributed 14.2pp of FY2026 growth and 66.0% of revenue [D470][D468].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, so incremental margin was 29.4% [D422][D421][D442].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well under the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The FY2026 margin slipped 0.2pp as operating costs grew 17.7% against 17.3% revenue growth [D433][D436][D421].
Higher infrastructure expenses to support cloud infrastructure growth drove the cloud and software margin down to 58.9% [D761][P16].
R&D fell to 15.3% of revenue, the window low, and added 1.9pp to margin [D399][D795][D444].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4%, helped by $1.5 billion of stock-based compensation tax benefits [D434][F54][D407][P9].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion, 1.88x net income, above the 1.58x window median [D426][F84][D408][D822].
The gain came from higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, as capex reached $55.7 billion, 82.6% of revenue [F104][D405][F94][D404].
Capex rose $34.4 billion, and capex now runs 7.30x D&A [P5][D410].
Net debt widened to $97.6 billion, equal to 145.0% of revenue, the 0th percentile against six software peers whose median net cash is 0.5% of revenue [D414][D415][D815][D816].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the latest burn [D412][D419].
Buybacks plus dividends were just $5.9 billion, and repurchases fell to $95 million [D416][X155].
Cash and investments cover only 1.3 years of the FY2026 burn, and $260 billion of additional data-center lease commitments sit off balance sheet [D419][P1].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for two years, at -1.39x in FY2026 against a 1.06x window median [D362][D409][D800].
Net debt rose for a second year to $97.6 billion as total debt grew 39.9% [D320][D367][D414][D440].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure by up to 0.60% [F44][X20].
If FY2027 capex falls below the FY2026 $55.7 billion, free cash flow should move back toward the 26.0% window median margin [F94][D794].
Watch operating margin against the 30.6% FY2026 level; a move back above the 32.2% median would confirm the cost trend reversed [F34][D788].
Watch net debt against $97.6 billion; further growth would keep the balance sheet at the 0th peer percentile [D414][D815].
